title: DDIM NLL via the probability-flow ODE: trace-estimated bits/dim without a variational bound
one_liner: The missing DDIM negative log-likelihood can be estimated — not as a bound but as an exact-in-the-limit density — by treating the DDIM sampler as the Euler discretization of the probability-flow ODE and evaluating the instantaneous change-of-variables formula with Hutchinson trace estimation.
description: The gap is that DDIM's deterministic sampler has no simple likelihood, so the authors skipped NLL entirely. The mechanism that fills it: DDIM's update is the Euler discretization of the VP probability-flow ODE, and for ODE-based generative models log p(x0) = log p(zT) − ∫ Tr(∂f/∂x) dt. The trace is tractable via Hutchinson's estimator (one backward-mode Jacobian-vector product per integrator step), so the same denoiser used for sampling can also yield per-sample NLL. This targets the implicit DDIM distribution itself rather than a variational upper bound, so it answers the exact question the authors left open. It also acts as a diagnostic: as the step count drops, the estimated log-Jacobian term should reveal when the deterministic map collapses toward a measure-zero set — explaining in quantitative terms why DDIM "doesn't present a simple way" of estimating likelihood.

sections.technique: Take a trained DDIM-compatible model (e.g., DDPM or score-based, VP noise schedule) on CIFAR-10 or ImageNet-32. (1) Define the drift f(x,t) of the probability-flow ODE corresponding to the DDIM schedule, or work directly with the discrete DDIM steps and their per-step Jacobians. (2) For held-out x0, integrate log p(zT) − ∫ Tr(∂f/∂x) dt along the reverse trajectory, estimating each trace as εᵀ J ε with ε ~ N(0,I) via one JVP per step; optionally add a control variate that subtracts a multiple of the identity, since the drift is nearly a scaled identity near x0. (3) Use the adjoint/checkpointed solver to avoid O(N) memory through N denoiser calls. (4) Validate first on a toy 2D Gaussian-mixture model with known density to measure bias and variance of the estimator vs number of JVP samples. (5) Report bits/dim for DDIM versus the DDPM ELBO on the same model, and plot estimated NLL against DDIM step count (10/20/50/100/1000) alongside FID, plus the per-step trace/rank of the Jacobian to localize where the map degenerates.
open_questions: Is the finite-step DDIM map a true diffeomorphism (so the discrete change-of-variables density is well-defined), or must NLL be defined only at the ODE limit — and does the answer change with step count?
How large is the Hutchinson estimator's variance on a full denoiser Jacobian at D ~ 3072+, and does one JVP per step suffice, or do control variates/Rademacher samples become necessary?
Are ODE-based exact NLL and the DDPM ELBO numerically comparable, or do they answer different questions (implicit deterministic density vs variational bound for a stochastic process)?
Does the trace estimate stay stable at low step counts (stiff ODE, larger Euler error), and can we separate the density of the discrete sampler from the density of the ODE it approximates?
Which drift parameterization is the right target — VP-ODE, sub-VP, or the literal discrete DDIM update — for the phrase 'the likelihood of DDIM'?
sections.rationale: The Neutral stance forbids swapping the gap's mechanism or bolting on a second idea; this candidate stays strictly on "estimate DDIM NLL" and only makes the vague part concrete by naming the standard machinery for ODE-based likelihoods (instantaneous change-of-variables + Hutchinson trace estimation). The diagnostic component (Jacobian collapse at low step counts) is the same idea's payoff, not a separate mechanism. Facts not in the supplied context, hence unverified here: that DDIM's update is the Euler discretization of the probability-flow ODE (Song et al., 2021); the instantaneous change-of-variables formula and its use in FFJORD/continuous normalizing flows; Hutchinson's trace estimator; and that the DDPM ELBO is computable whereas DDIM's is not. The numerical stability claims about control variates and adjoint solvers are likewise unverified.

_session.label: DDIM NLL via the probability-flow ODE: trace-estimated bits/dim without a variational bound
